messages:
AlertBot: [ALERT] High inbound request rate detected for /api/v1/generate from 4 regions. Aggregate ~1.2M req/min, 5xxs rising to 22%. Triggered at 1745032109

ajay: saw the alert. checking LB logs now. any pattern on IPs/UA?

maria_ops: quick scan: ~95% of requests have empty API key, same query param pattern, User-Agent 'okhttp/3.12.1' repeated. src IPs look distributed across ASNs (several cloud providers).

sam.sre: likely traffic abuse/scraping. autoscaling started but 5xxs spiked anyway. recommend immediate mitigations: 1) emergency per-IP rate limit on /api/v1/generate 2) deploy a temporary WAF rule to block known bot UA 3) drop malformed query param spikes.

ajay: +1. we should avoid full autoscale to zero-in on source. apply per-customer token bucket first. can someone push a quick WAF rule?

maria_ops: pushing a CloudFront WAF rule now (rate-based rule) — ripple time ~30s. rule: block if requests > 1000/min per IP for path /api/v1/generate.

sam.sre: instead of 1000/min per IP, use 120/min to be safer. most legitimate clients don't exceed that. lowering it to 120/min and add a whitelist for known partner IP ranges.

maria_ops: updating rule to 120/min + partner whitelist. applying.

product_ops: what's customer impact? do we risk blocking legitimate heavy users?

ajay: possible for some high-throughput partners. we'll add immediate temporary allowlist for partners with identified IP ranges and call them.

elaine_security: tagging incident as potential DDoS/traffic-abuse. we should collect PCAPs for a sample timeframe and enable enhanced audit logging for the gateway. also create a notice template for customers if they see errors.

sam.sre: created a short-term WAF rule:
```
AWS WAF RateBasedRule:
  Name: ddos-temp-2025-06
  Scope: CLOUDFRONT
  Match: URL path equals /api/v1/generate
  RateLimit: 7200 (120/min)
  Action: BLOCK
  Exclusions: allowlist for partner CIDRs
```

maria_ops: WAF rule active. signature shows incoming rate dropped ~85% within 60s. 5xxs trending down to 3%.

AlertBot: [INFO] Rule ddos-temp-2025-06 triggered 1.1M events in last 10m.

ajay: good. start blackholing top offending ASNs at the edge for now, and keep the WAF rule. sam, can you roll a more specific UA/blocklist rule to catch the okhttp pattern?

sam.sre: on it. pushing UA block and adding checks for empty API key header. also rate-limit by API key for authenticated traffic to avoid collateral.

product_ops: please prepare a short customer-facing message: impacted endpoint, what we did, whether keys were affected, remediation steps.

elaine_security: draft: "We detected a large volume of unauthenticated traffic to /api/v1/generate that caused transient errors for some customers. We deployed temporary WAF rules and per-IP rate limits to mitigate. No customer API keys were compromised. If you see 429s, retry with exponential backoff; contact support if issues persist."

product_ops: LGTM, will send to customers in 15 mins. include status page update and note about retries.

ajay: post-mortem action items: 1) convert temp WAF rule to a permanent, more targeted rule after 72h telemetry 2) add ASN + UA fingerprint alert to detect similar patterns earlier 3) update runbook to include partner allowlist flow and who to call 4) add per-route default rate limits in gateway (configurable per plan).

elaine_security: add: review audit logging retention for gateway (extend to 30d for traffic-abuse windows), and ensure WAF rule changes are audited. open follow-up ticket for KMS/key rotation? I don't think keys were involved.

sam.sre: creating incident ticket and assigning follow-ups. will include logs, ASNs, sample IPs, and the WAF rule id (ddos-temp-2025-06).

maria_ops: monitoring shows stable traffic now, 5xxs back to baseline. keeping mitigation rules for another 6 hours before relaxing.

ajay: thanks team. after we relax, let's run tabletop for DDoS response next week and update the SLO doc for throttling behavior. :thumbsup:

product_ops: message sent to affected customers and status page updated. closing comms after final verification.

AlertBot: [RESOLVED] Incident mitigation in place; rate of anomalies below threshold.

sam.sre: final note: add NF logs (ASN, UA, IP) to central ELK index for 90 days and schedule a post-incident review session Friday 10:00am.
